claims.description: Under fixed membership, a successful VerifyLeader quorum confirmation must not count positive notifications from Nonvoter members as substitutes for the voting-member support needed by its voter-majority threshold. In particular, self plus only nonvoter contributions cannot satisfy a threshold greater than one.

scope.description: Eligibility of support consumed for one public VerifyLeader future in a real leadership period, with fixed membership containing at least three voters and at least one nonvoter. Compare public completion with independently established eligibility of possible contributing peers.
assumptions: Non-Byzantine real target workers and correct in-memory transport/store behavior.
Unique validated member identities; no membership change, restart, user restore or leadership transfer during the checked interval.
The observer establishes absence of contributing remote voter replies for the selected future; inability to establish this is incomplete attribution, not a violation.
excluded: No assertion that VerifyLeader failure is necessary whenever current network reachability is low.
No requirement for eventual success, exact timing or a particular error.
No claim of stale application reads, divergent committed logs or crash durability.

parameters.success_condition: nil Error() on the correlated public future
parameters.forbidden_support: self plus only Nonvoter notifications when voter quorum is greater than one

claims.source: Candidate derived from attributed implementation responsibilities
pending: Construct and execute a real-worker comparison with independently correlated public completion and isolated support contributors.

grounding.derivation: The VerifyLeader API says it ensures the peer remains leader and can prevent stale FSM reads after leadership loss. Configuration defines nonvoters as recipients of replication excluded from elections and commitment; they cannot establish the electoral authority that the API checks. The implementation explicitly sets a voter-majority threshold and describes successful completion as a quorum agreeing it is still leader. The necessary eligibility condition is inferred from those responsibilities: adding replication-only peers cannot substitute for the electoral participants needed to confirm authority. This is a derived API support condition, not an assertion that every code guard is normative. Existing tests corroborate success with a connected voting majority and failure after leadership loss, but do not directly assert mixed-membership behavior.
grounding.applicability: Current VerifyLeader API, fixed mixed membership, no special recovery mode. The comparison concerns which contributions satisfy a future, not whether its local Leader state is still set or whether every successful reply was generated after invocation.
unresolved: Same-history contribution isolation and public completion still require trusted execution.
Broader stale-read consequence requires a separate observed newer decision and application endpoint.
alternatives: Voter-only lease checks may cause step-down and abort the future; the check must leave them running.
Negative verification notifications or leadership cleanup may prevent success; preserve these paths.
A real voter contribution could make success legitimate; such an execution cannot demonstrate the selected forbidden condition.
The single-voter fast path is legitimate and is outside this multi-voter scope.

associations.rationale: Binds the derived authority-check eligibility expectation to the registration and consumption path that could admit nonvoter support. API and suffrage are expectations; implementation and tests supply context and corroboration, not an observed violation.

bindings.description: Main-loop registration initializes a self vote, obtains voter quorum size, and registers every replication worker. Its boolean notifications reach verifyFuture.vote and then public completion in leaderLoop.
pending: Execution must identify actual eligible contributors and correlate future completion.
